companyDescription: Defense autonomy/robotics software · exclusive US manufacturing & distribution partnership with Israel Aerospace Industries for 'battle-proven' loitering munitions · FY26 revenue guided to grow 357-415% YoY
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Up 1.43% today, roughly mid-range within its 52-week band ($4.14-$10.80) as the market weighs genuinely fast revenue growth against real execution/timing risk on the IAI partnership's biggest contract opportunity.
summary: Palladyne AI has an exclusive US manufacturing and distribution partnership with Israel Aerospace Industries for 'battle-proven' loitering munitions — Northland specifically flagged this as a potential catalyst for a significant Department of War contract opportunity, and raised its target from $10 to $15 on the news. FY26 revenue guidance of $24-27M implies 357-415% YoY growth from 2025's $5.2M base, with a $17M backlog (most expected to convert over the next 12-18 months) providing real visibility. That said, real upside here has compressed: the 4-analyst average is $11.25 (+111%), and even Northland's raised $15 target is +181% — both fall short of this board's classic 200%+ bar, and Jefferies/Alliance Global have separately cut their targets, reflecting genuine analyst disagreement on execution timing.

catalysts.name: IAI Loitering Munitions Partnership — DoW Contract Potential
catalysts.description: Exclusive US manufacturing/distribution partnership with Israel Aerospace Industries for 'battle-proven' loitering munitions. Northland views this as a potential catalyst for a significant Department of War contract — the single biggest swing factor for the stock, though timing and scale remain unconfirmed.

catalysts.name: FY26 Revenue Ramp
catalysts.description: Guidance of $24-27M in FY26 revenue (357-415% YoY growth from $5.2M in 2025), backed by a $17M backlog as of Q1 2026, with most expected to convert to revenue over the next 12-18 months.

risks: Real upside has compressed below this board's typical 200%+ bar — the 4-analyst consensus is $11.25 (+111%), and even Northland's raised target ($15, +181%) doesn't quite clear it
Jefferies and Alliance Global have both cut their price targets, reflecting genuine, disclosed analyst disagreement on execution and contract-timing risk, not just conservative estimate variance
The DoW contract opportunity Northland flagged is still speculative — no confirmed award, size, or timeline yet
357-415% revenue growth guidance is off a very small base ($5.2M in 2025) — the percentage looks dramatic but the absolute dollar scale is still small relative to the market cap
Quarterly cash usage of $8-9M against a still-small revenue base means continued dependence on the backlog converting on schedule; a shelf registration remains in place for future capital needs

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holds at 3.50–3.75%, but new Chair Warsh's hawkish tone has 9 of 18 officials projecting a further 2026 hike, with the next FOMC decision Jul 28–29, 2026.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation remains above target and the 10-year yield sits near 4.48% — a headwind for a small-cap growth name still burning $8-9M/quarter against a small revenue base.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Defense-contract revenue is less directly rate-sensitive than pure-growth tech, but PDYN's small size and ongoing cash burn mean it's still exposed to the cost-of-capital channel via its standing shelf registration.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — the IAI partnership and any eventual DoW contract are policy/defense-budget driven and largely macro-independent, but PDYN's continued cash burn against a still-small revenue base means the financing environment still matters.
